findings: CAG-101 HIGH TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION — docs/architecture/solution-architecture.md:253-265, docs/architecture/adr/ADR-002-transactional-outbox.md:24-26, and docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:401-403. The publisher claims rows using SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishes, and then records the outcome, but the architecture never requires the claim transaction to commit and release locks before RabbitMQ I/O. It also does not explicitly place Geographic Reference calls before state-changing database transactions. Impact: remote I/O may occur while a database transaction or lock remains open, contrary to the required local transaction model. Required action: define unambiguous claim-commit-publish-outcome transactions and require all remote calls outside database transactions. Owner: solution-architecture-agent. Disposition: prevents PASS.

CAG-102 HIGH ADR_INCOMPLETE — docs/architecture/adr/ADR-001-reactive-single-deployable.md through ADR-005-database-managed-identifier-schemes.md. All five material ADRs omit mandatory Owner, Date or decision version, and explicit supersession relationship metadata. Rationale is distributed across drivers and consequences rather than recorded consistently, and ADR-005 does not use the same TO-BE decision classification as ADR-001 through ADR-004. Impact: decision ownership and lifecycle cannot be audited reliably. Required action: complete and normalize ADR metadata and decision lifecycle without changing the approved human requirements. Owner: solution-architecture-agent. Disposition: prevents PASS.

CAG-103 HIGH LIKEC4_MISSING — architecture/model.c4:35-69 and 153-157. The component view flattens API, application capabilities, outbound adapters, and bootstrap composition into one application container, but does not model the Domain or explicit core-owned port boundaries. Those major Clean Architecture boundaries exist only in docs/architecture/solution-architecture.md:109-136. Impact: the required LikeC4 source cannot independently demonstrate strict layer ownership, domain isolation, or port ownership. Required action: represent the domain, application, adapter, bootstrap, and core-owned port boundaries in LikeC4 with directional relations consistent with the approved dependency rules. Owner: solution-architecture-agent. Disposition: prevents PASS.

CAG-104 MEDIUM ARCHITECTURE_TRACEABILITY_GAP — docs/architecture/solution-architecture.md:470-481. The matrix groups broad requirement ranges and does not identify the controlling ADR, specific LikeC4 element or relation, component or port boundary, and validation method for each critical transaction, trust-boundary, and restricted-data flow. Impact: critical requirements cannot be followed end-to-end through decisions and modeled boundaries. Required action: extend critical traceability to the required requirement-to-decision-to-LikeC4-to-component-to-validation chain. Owner: solution-architecture-agent. Disposition: prevents PASS.

CAG-105 LOW NOT_RUN — Executable LikeC4 validation was unavailable. `npx --no-install likec4 validate` did not validate the model because likec4@1.59.2 was not installed locally. Manual structural review confirmed four required views, but syntax and rendering remain unverified. Required action: provide repository-controlled LikeC4 validation before quality-gate revalidation. Owner: architecture/tooling owner. Disposition: nonblocking by itself at the primary architecture gate.
